newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU says still pricing its wheat against U.S..
newsitem.headline: EU says still pricing its wheat against U.S..

text.p: The European Union is still pricing its wheat against U.S. wheat although U.S. prices now hardly reflect world markets, a senior EU grain official said on Friday.
But the EU, faced with a variety of U.S. prices, has some leeway in the way it values its wheat against U.S. wheat, he said.
"We maintained the same line. We have not changed our export policy," the official told Reuters.
"But there is some leeway in how we value (U.S. prices)," he added.
On Thursday the EU raised the refund on wheat exports to 16.59 Ecus per tonne from 15.97 Ecus last week, appearing to let EU prices undercut U.S. prices for the first time in months.
The subsidy priced EU wheat some five dollars below U.S. soft red winter wheat, analysts have said.
But the official estimated the 16.59 Ecus refund valued EU wheat for January at $158 per tonne, Fob, a level which was, he said, "in line, even slightly above U.S. wheat prices,".
He did not provide a comparison figure for U.S. wheat.

The EU has been under pressure from exporters and producers to stop pricing its wheat against tight U.S. markets and start competing with cheaper Argentine supplies. But the Commission has been reluctant to undercut U.S. wheat for fear of reviving a row over subsidies with the United States.
The official reckoned that although U.S. wheat prices were now out of line with world markets, the EU was still using them as a guideline when setting wheat export refunds.
"It (U.S. wheat) may not reflect world markets, but that's our guideline," he said.
The official explained that it was particularly tricky to try to compare U.S. and EU wheat prices because of the various premiums applying to U.S. wheat.
There were variations depending on whether the U.S. price chosen for comparison was Fob Gulf or Fob Pacific for soft white or hard red winter wheat, he said.
The EU until now has used soft red winter winter as a reference for calculating the refund applying to EU wheat exports, industry sources said.
But with three-fourths of the U.S. soft red winter crop already sold, these prices have lost their meaning, they said.
U.S prices reflecting actual transactions are currently those of hard red winter or soft white wheats.
